conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: I'm just feeling a bit off today. I caught a whiff of a fragrance that brought back a memory I just can't shake. It was like I was back in that moment, and it really threw me for a loop.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That sounds challenging. How did that experience affect your mood or thoughts after it happened?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: It got me all tangled up. I just kept replaying that memory over and over in my head, and I felt this heaviness sitting in my chest. It’s frustrating because I know it affects my focus and everything I try to do afterwards.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That sounds really difficult. How have you noticed that replaying the memory impacts your daily activities or interactions today?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: It makes everything feel like a struggle. I was trying to concentrate on work, but every time I thought I was getting into it, that memory would creep back in, and I'd just lose my place. It’s exhausting, and I find myself withdrawing more from conversations because I can't shake that feeling.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: It’s understandable that would be exhausting. When you were withdrawing from conversations, what did that feel like for you in the moment?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: It felt isolating, like I was stuck in my own head while everyone else was carrying on. I wanted to connect, but I just didn't have the energy to engage. I could feel that mix of frustration and sadness bubbling up, and instead, I just went quiet, hoping it would pass.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That sounds really tough. After you went quiet, did you notice any changes in how you felt or in your surroundings?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: Once I went quiet, it only felt heavier around me. There was this thick silence that made me even more aware of how disconnected I was. I could sense the chatter going on around me, but instead of it feeling comforting, it just emphasized how out of place I felt.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That makes a lot of sense. How did you cope with that feeling of disconnection during that time?
